Opens Android’s notification history, including entry points hidden by some phone manufacturers. If a manufacturer only hides the entry point, this app can try to open it. It cannot restore a removed feature or bypass system access restrictions. Usually, only notification messages from the last 24 hours are retained; the exact period depends on your phone.

First time? Turn on Use notification history on the system page; the name may vary by phone. Recording starts only after you enable it; notifications that disappeared before then cannot be recovered. If it has stayed on, you can view the records the system still retains.

Turning off Use notification history clears all saved history. Turning it back on starts recording again; cleared records will not return, and this app cannot recover them. Keep this system switch on to retain recent records. Closing this app does not turn off system recording.

Messages that never reached system notifications cannot be recorded or viewed here. This app does not read or save the history.

The shortcut opens notification history directly from your home screen in one tap, without opening this app first.

Tap Add shortcut to home screen, then follow any prompt from your home screen.

No prompt or icon? Some phones have a separate Home screen shortcuts permission. See the guidance in Shortcut settings. If your phone provides that switch, allow it, then return and try again.

If the icon already exists, use it. Some home screens may create duplicates if you add it again.

What it does
The main purpose of this app is to directly open Android’s built-in notification history when its entry point is hidden by the phone manufacturer. Add a home screen shortcut for one-tap access.

Compatibility
Not limited to Xiaomi or HyperOS. Your system must retain notification history and allow access to its page. If a manufacturer only hides the entry point, this app can try to open it. It cannot restore a removed feature or bypass system access restrictions.

Getting started
1. Tap Open notification history.
2. On first use, turn on Use notification history on the system page; the name may vary by phone.
3. Add a home screen shortcut if you want one-tap access.
Usually, only notification messages from the last 24 hours are retained; the exact period depends on your phone. Recording starts only after you enable it; notifications that disappeared before then cannot be recovered. If it has stayed on, you can view the records the system still retains.

Turning off Use notification history clears all saved history. Turning it back on starts recording again; cleared records will not return, and this app cannot recover them. Keep this system switch on to retain recent records. Closing this app does not turn off system recording.

When it can help
• Recalled messages: revisit a WeChat or QQ notification if the original message produced one before being recalled and the system still retains it.
• Mentions: check who mentioned you when that information appears in the notification.
• Message previews: for example, view the text retained in a BOSS Zhipin notification without entering the chat. It may show more than a banner preview, but the full message is not guaranteed.
In the user-tested setup, viewing only system notification history without entering the BOSS Zhipin chat did not mark messages as read. Behavior may change after app or system updates; check again if needed. Avoid tapping notification entries or replying, as this may open the source app or change message status.

Requirements and limits
Messages that never reached system notifications cannot be recorded or viewed through this tool. Missing, hidden or truncated text cannot be reconstructed. A messaging app may not post a notification while its chat is open.
To improve the chance of retaining a notification before recall, keep WeChat, QQ and other messaging apps connected, allow their notifications and let them receive messages in the background. Check their battery and background restrictions if needed. Being online alone does not guarantee a notification for every message.
You do not need to keep this app open. It is not a complete anti-recall tool: it does not prevent recalls or recover messages the system never recorded.

How it works and privacy
Android stores the notifications, not this app. This app does not read, import, search or upload messages, modify WeChat or QQ, or need internet access. Normal use does not require developer mode or a computer connection.

Permissions
Use notification history enables system recording; it does not grant this app notification access. Home screen shortcuts is a separate permission on some phones; others may only ask you to confirm adding. This app does not need notification access, floating windows or background pop-ups.
